COURSE SYLLABUS
PART I: COURSE SPECIFICATION
Course Code and Name 	: 	CSC 103 - Discrete Structures 2 	Credit Units: 	Lecture: 2 units 	Laboratory: 1
Pre-requisite/ Co-requisite : 	Pre-req: CSC 102 - Discrete Structures 1 	Total Contact Hours: 	36 hours lecture : 54 hours laboratory
Effectivity 	: 	2nd Semester A.Y. 2025-2026 	Learning Modality 	: 	Onsite/ Online (Blended Learning)
Learning Resources Needed : 	Classroom, Audio-visual, Laptop, Internet 	Outcomes-Based Evidence : 	At least 80% of the class attain > 60% on all CO
Course Description: This course builds upon the foundational concepts introduced in Discrete Structures 1, extending students’ understanding of discrete mathematics as applied to computer
science and computing systems. It focuses on advanced topics, including number theory, combinatorics, recurrence relations, probability theory, graph theory, and automata and formal languages.
Key topics include divisibility, prime numbers, modular arithmetic, the Euclidean algorithm, public-key cryptography (RSA), counting principles, the pigeonhole principle, recurrence relations,
probability on finite sample spaces, graph properties, and finite automata. Through guided problem-solving, laboratory activities, and performance-based assessments, students develop analytical
thinking, algorithmic reasoning, and modeling skills essential for advanced computing courses. A blended learning approach is employed, utilizing MASAOLms and face-to-face sessions, with
assessments that include quizzes, laboratory activities, and major examinations.
PART II: VISION, MISSION, Graduate Attributes, Institutional Outcomes, PEO, PO, CO
Vision 	Mission
A socially-engaged, digital, innovation, and entrepreneurial university excelling globally in
science, engineering, and the arts by 2028.
As a transformative university, CSU is a responsible steward of problem-solvers and value
creators who are driven to create a sustainable future for the region, the nation, and beyond.
Graduate Attributes 	Institutional Outcomes
Caraga State University graduates manifest the virtue of a CSUAN:
Competent,
Socially-engaged,
Upright,
Agile and Innovative, and
Nurturing Leaders.
The CSUAN graduate is globally competent, lifelong learner, visionary steward,
sustainability-advocate, morally-upright, ethically critical, with integrity, adaptable to change,
innovative, has entrepreneurial mindset, and a transformative leader.
IO1. Transformative Leadership and Stewardship. A CSUAN applies advanced expertise in
addressing complex societal challenges as a transformative leader and purpose-driven steward.
IO2. Research, Innovation and Enterprise. A CSUAN produces quality research outputs,
applies innovative thinking, and develops entrepreneurial solutions that address regional and
global issues, in pursuit of sustainability and economic advancement.
IO3. Lifelong Learning and Social Responsibility. A CSUAN continually enhances their
knowledge and skills, and actively contributes to community development while exemplifying
social responsibility, ethical standards, and the core values of Caraga State University.

modular arithmetic. 	E 	E 	E 	E 	1,5,7 	1 	4,9

3 Weeks
● Apply divisibility rules to determine properties of
integers.
● Compute the GCD and LCM of integers using
the Euclidean Algorithm.
● Use the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic to
express integers as products of primes.
● Apply congruence relations and modular
arithmetic to solve computational problems.
● Demonstrate basic number-theoretic concepts
used in public-key cryptosystems (RSA) through
guided examples.

PART IV. GRADING SYSTEM
The following table is used to assess student performance:
Grade Status 	Disposition
Grade in all course outcomes is greater than 60% 	Pass. Refer to the grading table for the equivalent numerical grade
Average is greater than 60% but at least 1 of the
course outcomes are with grade less than 60%
Implement intervention/ conduct removal exam/ require additional
assessment. The final grade is based on the original average.
Average is lesser than 60% but 50% or more of the
outcomes are attained.
Implement intervention/ conduct removal exam/ require additional
assessment. The highest grade obtained after passing the outcome is 3.0
Average is lesser than 60% and more than 50% of
the number of course outcomes did not attain > 60%
Failed. 5.0

Class Policies and Important Reminders
● Rubrics are presented to the class or given together with the instructions for a particular Assessment. You may ask your instructor for the rubrics in case they were not provided prior to the
project-based assessment, essay, case study, etc.
● Any student proven to have committed fraud, following due process, shall receive a failing grade for the course.
● Refer to the student handbook for the code of conduct inside/ outside the classroom.

33487-2742: CRC Press Taylor &amp; Francis Group.
● David, L. (2018). Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science. John Wiley &amp; Sons.
● Hademenos, G. J.; Lipschutz, S. (2003). Discrete mathematics: Based on Schaum's outline of theory and problems of discrete mathematics, second edition, by Seymour Lipschutz,
Ph. D. and Marc Lars Lipson, Ph. D. New York: McGraw-Hill.
● Jenkyns, T. A.; Stephenson, B. (2018). Fundamentals of Discrete Math for Computer Science A Problem-Solving Primer. Cham: Springer International Publishing.
● Johnsonbaugh, R. (2019). Discrete mathematics. NY, NY: Pearson.
